data.narrative:
Valthos, a Seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Kathleen McMahon and Tess van Stekelenburg, has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 10 private companies (including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, and Shield AI) and 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS), all operating in the same sector at Seed or Series A stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $30M raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier, yields $75M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—UFORCE ($1.0B, Seed), Singularity ($400M, Series A), and NODA AI ($125M, Series A)—produces a median valuation of $400M, with a range spanning $125M to $1.0B.

The two methods produce materially divergent signals. Triangulating both approaches yields a range of $64M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $238M. The wide dispersion reflects significant uncertainty around which comparable peer set most accurately anchors Valthos's profile. Key drivers of range sensitivity include the degree to which Seed-stage capital raised correlates to post-money valuation in this sector, and whether UFORCE's $1.0B valuation represents a sector-wide pricing norm or an outlier. Stage progression alone may underweight market conditions; peer medians may not fully account for Valthos's specific competitive positioning or capital efficiency relative to comparables.
